source.title: Feature Integration Spaces: Joint Training Reveals Dual Encoding in Neural Network Representations

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own SAE/NFM reconstruction and behavioral-intervention results, and argues that SAE identity features alone miss meaningful computational structure. This refines and challenges an identity-only account; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and other work, but cited findings are not extracted as results. It does not sweep feature sparsity, feature importance, or feature-to-dimension ratios to test the toy-model transition or capacity account. Training settings and feature-selection criteria are not treated as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study argues that SAE features alone miss structure, a point bearing on V5's completeness. It tests this by showing that SAE reconstruction residuals and KL pathology in OpenLLaMA-3B are partly predictable from the SAE's own features. The evidence is confounded: the added NFM has many extra parameters, and 95% of the gain comes from a linear map of SAE features. It does not test toy-model superposition, the capacity account, or 1-D features.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also argue that persistent polysemanticity may reflect compressed feature-integration information rather than capacity artifacts. They also claim joint training spontaneously yields bimodal feature norms, with low-norm features feeding integration pathways.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies toy networks with controlled feature sparsity and importance; this study trains SAE/NFM architectures on OpenLLaMA-3B activations and evaluates reconstruction, KL divergence, feature organization, and interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports differences between sequential and joint training, between linear and nonlinear components, and between the tested integration feature 4022 and control feature 1113; linear-component clamping does not show the interaction observed for feature 4022.

fits_no_version.finding: Clamping secondary-SAE feature 4022 of the NFM embedding produced a formality×emotion interaction in reconstructed logits (F=5.06, p=0.027). Linear components and feature 1113 showed no interaction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonlinear combinations of SAE features carry behaviourally relevant 'integration' structure not captured by SAE identity features.

record.problems: Proof of concept is limited to one 3B model and one stated layer. The authors note scale constraints, difficulty interpreting integration features, and that maximum-activation analysis did not yield interpretable patterns for them. Behavioral validation uses a designed stimulus set and selected features; the text says the counterfactual exploration is not exhaustive.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported outcomes left out. Cited results from other work and parameter or hyperparameter values used only to configure the experiments were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry test. The Gram matrix analysis concerns SAE dictionaries, not superposition in a model.
No manipulation or measurement of capacity pressure or feature importance.
The paper argues polysemanticity may encode feature integration rather than capacity artifacts, but measures no neuron polysemanticity. This is argument only.
The SAE is used as a tool. There is no test of features being spread across neurons, or of recoverable sparse features beyond training fit.
Stability across seeds or runs and canonicality are not tested. Only completeness of reconstruction and KL is addressed.
No comparison of 1-D directions with multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Control: a secondary SAE trained directly on the original SAE residuals gave no significant added reconstruction, unlike the NFM. This bears on whether the residual structure is just more dictionary features.

Joint training changes the dictionary's squared-norm distribution from unimodal (mean 0.395) to bimodal (means about 0.05 and 0.37). This weakly bears on SAE features depending on the training objective (canonicality).
missing.locator: Feature Orthogonality and Emergent Specialization; Figure 4

record.verdict_notes: Single model, single layer, single author. Several factors weaken the incompleteness claim. The SAE-only baseline in the sequential comparison (K=250, error 0.38) is much worse than the Stage-1 SAE (loss 0.136). The NFM adds substantial parameters. Most of the gain is linear in SAE features. The 'AAAI 2025' peer-review status in the record is not stated in the text. The intervention results concern the study's own architecture.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network overcapacity experiment, sparsity-dependent transition, or test of regular superposition geometry. The reported SAE Gram-matrix analysis is not a test of the stated toy-model claim.
No manipulation or measurement of capacity pressure, feature importance, or whether important features obtain dedicated dimensions while others share.
The paper proposes computational integration as an explanation for some apparent polysemanticity, but does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE-derived features in one model and layer; does not measure whether features are spread across many neurons or establish this across LLMs.

Tests whether SAE-only reconstructions omit behaviorally and reconstructively relevant integration structure. Does not test feature stability across training runs or whether SAE features are canonical units in general.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multi-dimensional feature representations as the units of superposition.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured primary SAE reconstruction on activations from layer 16.
rows.measure: Primary SAE reconstruction loss and variance explained
rows.locator: Model and Data Configuration; Stage 1: Sparse Autoencoder Training
rows.note: Shows an SAE decomposition of this model's activations with substantial, but not complete, variance explained.
rows.check: This is the training performance of the study's tool (primary SAE), a setup value. It is not a test of V4: there is no measure of whether recovered features are interpretable or sparse beyond what training imposed.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Compared sequential SAE+NFM reconstruction with SAE-only reconstruction.
rows.note: The additional integration component improves over the SAE-only reconstruction, contrary to treating the SAE-only representation as complete for reconstruction.
rows.check: The state should be partial, not reversed. The SAE-only baseline restricts top-K to 250, and its error (0.38) is far worse than the Stage-1 SAE loss (0.136), so the baseline may be handicapped. This is the study's own method compared with the SAE, with extra parameters added.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Compared sequential SAE+NFM reconstruction with SAE-only reconstruction.
rows.note: The additional integration component improves over the SAE-only reconstruction.
rows.check: Same as r2. Incompleteness is shown only relative to a handicapped, lower-parameter baseline. The linear NFM part (95.5% of the gain) is just another linear readout of SAE features.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Compared sequential SAE+NFM with the SAE baseline on pathological KL divergence.
rows.measure: KL divergence relative to the stated random-error baseline; reduction in pathological divergence
rows.note: The paper describes the SAE+NFM change as a reduction in pathological divergence.
rows.check: The relevant fact is the SAE-only KL of 2.99x the random-error baseline, which shows SAE reconstruction is not behaviourally complete. The 29.8% reduction is the study's own method's performance. The state should be partial, not reversed.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Compared joint SAE+NFM reconstruction with SAE-only reconstruction.
rows.value: Joint model reconstruction error: 0.162; 41.3% improvement over SAE
rows.note: Joint integration components improve reconstruction relative to the SAE-only result.
rows.check: Joint-training comparison with a 496M-parameter architecture versus the SAE. The gain is confounded by added capacity. Partial, not reversed.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Clamped secondary SAE integration feature 4022 and measured logit effects across a 2×2 formality-by-emotion stimulus design.
rows.note: The authors report a significant nonadditive behavioral interaction from clamping an integration feature. This supports the presence of behaviorally relevant structure beyond the identity-only reconstruction, but does not establish that SAE features are stable or canonical.
rows.check: This clamps a secondary-SAE feature of the study's own NFM embedding and reads reconstructed logits. It concerns the study's add-on, not whether SAE features are the model's units. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Clamped linear integration weights and compared logits with baseline.
rows.note: Control indicates the reported nonlinear behavioral interaction was not observed for the linear-component clamping comparison.
rows.check: Control for the study's own method (linear NFM components). It has no bearing on a version.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Clamped secondary SAE feature 1113 and measured effects across categories.
rows.measure: Systematic category patterns; F and p values
rows.value: No systematic patterns; F>0.28, p>0.18 for all clamping ranges
rows.note: The paper identifies this as a non-sensitive-feature control.
rows.check: Control feature from the study's own secondary SAE; no bearing on a version. The text also reports F=0.022, p=0.996 for feature 1113 sensitivity.

rows.subject: OpenLLaMA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured joint-architecture KL-divergence improvement by component.
rows.measure: KL-divergence improvement over the SAE comparison
rows.baseline: SAE comparison; exact baseline value not stated
rows.note: The joint integration components reduce the reported KL divergence errors relative to the SAE comparison.
rows.check: Component KL improvements of the study's own architecture over the SAE. The SAE baseline value is not stated. Of the improvement, 50.9% is linear, which a better linear decoder could also achieve. Partial, not reversed.

relationships.condition: OpenLLaMA-3B layer 16, WikiText-103, sequential and joint SAE+NFM
relationships.reason: SAE-only KL is 2.99x the random-error baseline, and residuals are 23–41% predictable from SAE features (r2–r5, r9). Baselines are handicapped and capacity is unmatched, so incompleteness is shown only weakly.
relationships.display_finding: SAE-only KL was 2.99x the random-error baseline and residuals were 23–41% predictable from SAE features, though handicapped baselines and unmatched capacity make this weak evidence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The primary SAE explains 86.4% of activation variance, and the study identifies SAE-derived semantic features; see r1.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: OpenLLaMA-3B, layer 16; sequential and joint SAE+NFM results
reader_labels.reason: Additional integration components improve reconstruction and reduce reported KL divergence errors, indicating that the SAE-only feature representation does not capture all relevant structure; see r2–r5 and r9.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: Clamping integration feature 4022 produces a significant nonadditive behavioral effect, while the stated controls do not; see r6–r8.
